html:
In 2 CE the Han dynasty counted the people of its empire. The census recorded about 58 million people in some 12 million households, one of the oldest surviving counts of a large population anywhere.

The Han state needed the numbers to tax households and draft men for labour and the army. Officials recorded each household, and the totals for every commandery were kept in the Book of Han, the official history written by Ban Gu and his family. The figures show that most people then lived in the north, on the plains of the Yellow River.

The census caught the Han at a peak. A few years later Wang Mang seized the throne, and floods and civil war followed. Later counts in the Eastern Han were lower and showed more people living further south, a shift that grew stronger after the flight south of the 300s. The Roman Empire of the same years probably had a similar number of people.
sum: In 2 CE the Han dynasty counted the people of its empire. The census recorded about 58 million people in some 12 million households, one of the oldest surviving counts of a large population anywhere.
